doc.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023

title: Converting to Islam and views on God
summary: He explains his conversion through belief in the oneness of God, contrasting Christianity and Judaism.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Well said. Am I correct that you adopted the Muslim religion at some point?
Was there something in society that was happening at the time or —
I’ll tell you right now before you ask me —

What it is, it was the idea, the clarity of the oneness of God you know. To me God is singular you know. And I had no partners, and Christianity — well Judaism is that way. They, you know, it’s just God that’s it. But Christianity got three Gods. Now they say it’s one God but in three parts you know. And then the one part is his son, one part is the holy spirit. But I don’t think the almighty God would need a son you know. What do you need a son for you’re almighty and merciful. The almighty, he’s perfectly capable of being a savior, for showing mercy he made the sun and the moon and the stars and everything else. He’s perfectly capable of redeeming you if you need redemption you know. So you know that said but I found that the good aspects of most religions you know, in Hinduism they’ve got a trinity too, but then they’ve got many other gods. But it’s not a Catch-22 word but it’s a loaded word you know, because whatever the name of the diety is that’s on most high, it wouldn’t be in English or any language of human beings anyway because you know God is above a human being, way above it. I think there was Mohammed, peace be upon him, that asked somebody — they was out one night and he said, “Hey, man.” He says, “Yeah, what?” He said, “You see all that out there?” He said, “Yeah.” He said, “What do you think is easier to make, to make that or to make you?” You know? And he had to say, “To make me” you know. Rather than make all that you know. And he didn’t have the slightest clue how much that was, how full it was, how huge it was you know, but see we have to use first person singular. That’s why we say him or his you know. And that’s what we call a big ship a she or her you know, because it’s greater than © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

the average human being but it ain’t greater, it’s far, far away from it you know, the way I look at it. And when he says well he made man in his own image I say, “Yeah man got an image of his own” so you know he made man in his own image, not in his image, not in my image. I don’t have no image you know. If I had an image how could you compose it in a human being? You mean to tell me the guy that made Venus, whoever made Venus, Pluto, Neptune, Mars, and Andromeda, the galaxy, has got two hands and two eyes and a tongue and eat and use the bathroom you know? What is he, a million miles tall you know? You know that’s crazy. And if he’s like a man and has got a son, he don’t have no wife, they say well no, he don’t need no wife, he can just have a son you know, or do what he wants. I said yeah, you don’t need a son either, but it gets to be like that because of our language. But Judaism is closes to it. You know it’s the same thing actually because Ishmael and who’s the other one — the brothers of Abraham and his two sons.
In the Old Testament you mean?
Yeah. When Sara sent the handmaid away with the boy, the two boys got separated so their language changed you know. So the one who was with Abraham — was it Isaac?

But anyway he would say, “Shalom [inaudible] and then Ishmael said, “Shalom Le Chiem” you know. The language got compromised you know, on both sides. But it’s really the same. Migrants, you know, the Arabic-speaking [inaudible] and the Jewish one was saying [inaudible]. I don’t want to get in an argument about that. That’s why I don’t stretch it, but to me if there is a God there can be no comparisons whatsoever. When they say we’ll reach out and touch the face of God — that’s symbolic you know. You know that’s an analogy. That’s a metaphor you know. God don’t have no face but he got a beard too? He got teeth you know? He got 20/20 vision, 360 degree vision but both his eyes face forward you know? They’re thinking about Zeus and Atlas you know and [inaudible] and people like that and personas like that.
